newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Held Maltese tanker leaves Venezuela.
newsitem.headline: Held Maltese tanker leaves Venezuela.

text.p: The Maltese flagged tanker Plate Princess, held in Venezuela since late May after it spilt 20 barrels of oil in Lake Maracaibo, has been allowed to leave the country, shipping authorities said.
The boat left for Cuba on Saturday, Maracaibo port captain Jose Fernandez told Reuters, "because the penal judge lifted the embargo on the boat ... after the owners posted guarantees in the courts."
Venezuela is a member of the Civil Liabilities Convention, which covers compensation from oil spills

However, the Greek-flagged tanker Nissos Amargos, which spilt 25,000 barrels of oil on Feb 28, is still being held by Venezuela although P & I clubs, which represents the ship's owners, has posted guarantees with the courts.
The long delay of the two ships' release has raised concern among international shipping agencies and insurers.
